description:
Figure 5, titled "The average likes of headlines from different season groups," is a composite figure consisting of four distinct charts that analyze the relationship between text similarity, user interaction, and popularity.

The first chart is a line graph plotting "Avg. similarity (10e-2)" on the y-axis against "Δ Days" on the x-axis. The data points, connected by a light blue line, show a general downward trend, starting at a similarity of approximately 1.85 (185) and decreasing to around 1.70 (170) across the range of Δ Days, which is divided into four intervals: (0,90], (90,180], (180,270], and (270,360], (360,450].

The second chart is a bar graph with "Most similar group of posts" on the x-axis and "Avg. Like #" on the y-axis. It displays four bars representing different groups, with average likes ranging from approximately 480 to 540. The bar for the (270,360] group has the highest average likes, while the (90,180] group has the lowest.

The third chart is a bar graph with "Category" on the x-axis and "Avg. similarity" on the y-axis. It compares two categories: "different users" and "same user." The bar for "different users" is very short, with a value close to 0.00, while the bar for "same user" is significantly taller, with a value of approximately 0.11.

The fourth chart is a line graph with "PSI" on the x-axis and two y-axes on the right side. The left y-axis is labeled "Avg. popularity" and the right y-axis is labeled "std-error." Two lines are plotted: a light blue line for "Avg. popularity" and a red dashed line for "std-error." The "Avg. popularity" line shows a peak around a PSI value of 0.4, reaching approximately 6.3, and then decreases. The "std-error" line shows a general increasing trend as PSI increases.
